physical_harm: Eleven injuries including incised wounds, brain damage, and fractures
number_of_offences: 13 offences charged, 3 upheld by trial court, 2 acquitted by High Court
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the testimony of PW-1 as the sole eye-witness but emphasized the need for heightened scrutiny due to the improbable nature of the injuries and the circumstances surrounding her statement.
witness_credibility: The court doubted the credibility of PW-1, noting that her deposition did not contain the entire truth and that her statement was inconsistent between the FIR and her court statement. The court also questioned the reliability of PW-8 as an eye-witness due to his absence at the time of the occurrence.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 16.06.1995; Trial judgment: 18.07.2008; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: August 06, 2009
legal_representation: S. R. Singh, Ram Naresh Yadav, Vikrant Yadav, Krishna K. Yadav, Aadarsh Kumar Verma, Shivam Sharma, V. Sushant Gupta, Advs. for the Appellants; Deepak Thukral, Dr. Monika Gusain, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted three persons; High Court: Acquitted one of the accused while upholding the conviction of the two appellants; Supreme Court: Acquitted the appellants
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that PW-1 and PW-8 were eye-witnesses to the occurrence, and that appellant no.2 made the fatal assault on the head of the deceased with a lathi while appellant no.1 also assaulted the deceased. They emphasized the existence of a street light and the credibility of PW-1 as an eye-witness due to her relationship with the deceased.
defence_argument: The defence submitted that once the other accused have been acquitted, the two appellants alone cannot be convicted with the aid of Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code. They argued that there is no evidence of any common intention, and that PW-1 and PW-8 were not eye witnesses as they reached the scene after the occurrence.
legal_principle_applied: Conviction on the basis of a solitary eye-witness is sustainable if there is reliable evidence cogent and convincing along with surrounding circumstances, but such evidence calls for heightened scrutiny.
precedent_relied_upon: State of Rajasthan v. Bhola Singh and Anr., AIR 1994 SC 542; Lallu Manjhi and another v. State of Jharkhand, (2003) 2 SCC 401; Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1953 SC 364; Sakharam Nangare v. State of Maharashtra, (2012) 9 SCC 249; Khem Karan and others v. State of U.P. and another, (1974) 4 SCC 603
other_sentence_order: The appellants are acquitted. They are directed to be released forthwith if they are not required in any other case. In the event of having been released on bail, their bail bonds shall stand discharged.
